title: Cyclists: Passing, Lanes & the Dutch Reach
whatItIs: Cyclists are among the road users most at risk and are often hard to see. Give them space, look out for them, and open doors with care.
keyFacts: When passing a cyclist, leave at least 1.5 metres at speeds up to 30 mph, and more at higher speeds.
If you can't leave that much space, wait behind until you can.
Don't cut across cyclists going straight ahead when you turn or change lane.
Cyclists may ride in the middle of the lane on quiet roads, in slow traffic and at junctions, so they can be seen.
Open your car door with the hand furthest from it (the "Dutch reach"), so you turn and look for cyclists.

items.label: Minimum gap at up to 30 mph
items.note: Leave more space at higher speeds

items.label: Cyclists may ride side by side
items.note: Can be safer for groups on narrow or quiet roads

items.label: The Dutch reach: open your door with it
items.note: It makes you turn and look behind

a.label: Cyclist in the middle of the lane
points: Allowed on quiet roads and at junctions

b.label: Cyclist near the side of the road
points: Still leave at least 1.5 m up to 30 mph
May swerve round drains or potholes

onTheTest.question: You are passing a cyclist on a 30 mph road. What is the minimum space you should leave?
onTheTest.why: Leave at least 1.5 metres at speeds up to 30 mph, and more when you are going faster.

traps: 1.5 m is the minimum up to 30 mph, not the gap for every speed.
Riding two abreast is allowed: don't squeeze past.
At an advanced stop line, stop at the first white line and leave the cyclists' box clear.
